items.title: Capcom confirms data breach affecting 11.7 million accounts
items.snippet: Japanese gaming giant Capcom has confirmed that hackers breached its membership service, CAPCOM ID, exposing more than 11.7 million customer email addresses and associated information. [...]
items.summary: Capcom confirms hackers breached its CAPCOM ID membership service, exposing customer email addresses and associated information.
items.why: Review account data exposure and notify affected users through established incident-response processes.

items.title: Arista patches new VeloCloud Orchestrator zero-day exploited in attacks

items.summary: Arista released updates for an actively exploited zero-day vulnerability affecting VeloCloud Orchestrator On-Prem deployments.
items.why: Check for affected On-Prem deployments and apply the security updates.

items.title: Attackers Exploit Third VeloCloud Orchestrator Zero-Day in Four Months
items.snippet: The critical-severity SQL injection flaw allows attackers to access privileged internal functionality and gain operator privileges. The post Attackers Exploit Third VeloCloud Orchestrator Zero-Day in Four Months appeared first on SecurityWeek .
items.summary: The critical SQL injection flaw in VeloCloud Orchestrator allows attackers to access privileged internal functionality and gain operator privileges.
items.why: Check VeloCloud Orchestrator for exposure and apply available security fixes.

items.title: Critical Flaw in Python’s Popular Pillow Image Library Allows Code Execution via a Crafted Image
items.snippet: Pillow, the most widely used image library for Python, can be made to run operating system commands on a server by specifying the name of a file it is told to open. The flaw, CVE-2026-112900, is in the way Pillow handles EPS images, which it opens by passing the file's name to Ghostscript, a separate program it runs to
items.summary: A flaw in Pillow’s handling of EPS images can allow operating system commands to run on a server when it opens a specified file.
items.why: Check servers that use Pillow to open EPS images and review file-handling safeguards.

items.title: Researchers Demonstrate Node2Shell RCE Exploit on Node.js Build Using Crafted Brotli Data
items.snippet: Malicious Brotli data can make an application on an official build of Node.js run attacker-supplied code, security researchers at Imperva have demonstrated. Their "Node2Shell" proof of concept ran code on the official Node.js 24.22.0 image for Linux arm64, with no debugger or custom build, by feeding crafted data to th
items.summary: Researchers demonstrated that malicious Brotli data can make an application on an official Node.js build run attacker-supplied code.
items.why: Check how applications process Brotli data and monitor for unexpected code execution.

items.title: Critical x402 SDK Flaw Could Let Malicious APIs Drain AI Agents’ Token Balances
items.snippet: AI agents paying for API calls with the x402 SDKs could sign a payment for their full balance of a supported token if a malicious API asked for it, security firm V12 said on October 22. The cause was the SDKs' default client, which set no spending limit until releases on August 18 added one. The risk was limited to age
items.summary: Security firm V12 says a malicious API could ask x402 SDK clients to sign payments for their full balance of a supported token.
items.why: Check x402 SDK payment limits before allowing AI agents to pay APIs.

items.title: Quest Diagnostics Reports Cyber Breach Affecting ‘Certain Patient Records’
items.snippet: In a regulatory filing, Quest Diagnostics reported unauthorized access to its Quanum Lab Services Manager, a platform where certain clients can place test orders. The post Quest Diagnostics Reports Cyber Breach Affecting ‘Certain Patient Records’ appeared first on SecurityWeek .
items.summary: Quest Diagnostics reported unauthorized access to Quanum Lab Services Manager, where certain clients can place test orders.
items.why: Check access to lab-service platforms and review records for unauthorized activity.

items.title: LiteLLM Compromised in Fresh Supply Chain Attack
items.snippet: Hackers used compromised GitHub CLI OAuth tokens to push and approve malicious packages on PyPI and Docker. The post LiteLLM Compromised in Fresh Supply Chain Attack appeared first on SecurityWeek .
items.summary: SecurityWeek reports hackers used compromised GitHub CLI OAuth tokens to push and approve malicious packages on PyPI and Docker.
items.why: Review OAuth token access and verify packages and approvals in software supply chains.

items.title: Atlassian Patches 75 Flaws in Data Center and Server Products
items.snippet: Atlassian’s October bulletin lists 176 vulnerability entries, including 14 critical-severity issues, all in third-party components. The post Atlassian Patches 75 Flaws in Data Center and Server Products appeared first on SecurityWeek .
items.summary: Atlassian’s October bulletin lists 176 vulnerability entries, including 14 critical-severity issues in third-party components; the title says it patched 75 flaws.
items.why: Check affected Data Center and Server products and prioritize relevant third-party component updates.

items.title: PHP2Shell Exploit Attempts Hit Millions as Attackers Try to Deploy Mirai Malware
items.snippet: Threat actors have been observed unsuccessfully attempting to exploit the newly disclosed PHP2Shell vulnerabilities to rope infected systems into a Mirai botnet variant called Potassium, as it emerges that weaponizing the flaws may be harder than previously thought. The attacks aim to exploit CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-20
items.summary: Researchers observed unsuccessful attempts to exploit PHP2Shell vulnerabilities to add systems to a Mirai botnet variant called Potassium.
items.why: Check for PHP2Shell exploitation attempts and review exposed systems for signs of compromise.

items.title: Pentagon, Lockheed agree to decade-long F-35 framework deal for hundreds of jets
items.snippet: The tentative agreement, which still needs lawmakers’ blessing, covers production and sustainment over the 10 years.

items.why: The framework concerns long-term fighter production and sustainment.

items.summary: The Spanish Navy and Navantia are developing an F110 IAMD frigate, an evolution of the Bonifaz class with integrated air and missile defense capabilities.

items.summary: The UK Ministry of Defence is proposing to redevelop Cawdor Barracks as the UK host site for the DARC radar programme.

items.title: USAF Confirms Bombers Could Have A Major Air-To-Air Combat Role
items.snippet: Bombers are now being viewed as another potential air-to-air asset on top of growing the fighter fleet and establishing a CCA force. The post USAF Confirms Bombers Could Have A Major Air-To-Air Combat Role appeared first on TWZ .
items.summary: The War Zone reports that the USAF sees bombers as a potential air-to-air asset, alongside expanding the fighter fleet and establishing a CCA force.
items.why: A possible air-to-air role could affect how bombers contribute to combat operations.

items.title: Are yearlong deployments the Navy’s new normal?
items.snippet: That's what officials are telling sailors' families in Japan, where two destroyers are slated for 12- and 14-month cruises.
items.summary: Officials are telling sailors’ families in Japan that two destroyers are slated for 12- and 14-month cruises.
items.why: Longer cruises may affect deployment planning and sailors’ families.

items.title: Four KJ-3000 Radar Jets At Chinese Factory Point To Serial Production
items.snippet: The KJ-3000 is the most capable of China’s rapidly expanding airborne early warning and control aircraft fleet. The post Four KJ-3000 Radar Jets At Chinese Factory Point To Serial Production appeared first on TWZ .
items.summary: The War Zone says four KJ-3000 radar jets at a Chinese factory point to serial production. It describes the aircraft as China’s most capable airborne early warning and control aircraft.
items.why: The aircraft fleet’s expansion is relevant to airborne surveillance and control capabilities.

items.title: Space Force shifts into high gear on cislunar warfare, with RFIs coming soon
items.snippet: Maj. Gen. Stephen Purdy, the Space Force’s portfolio acquisition executive for advanced programs, said the service wants to field cislunar capabilities by the end of fiscal 2029.
items.summary: Breaking Defense reports that the Space Force wants to field cislunar capabilities by the end of fiscal 2029, according to Gen. Stephen Purdy.
items.why: Cislunar capabilities extend military planning into the space between Earth and the Moon.

items.title: Israel preparing full lockdown of occupied West Bank after Hebron gunfight
items.snippet: Clampdown comes as Israeli pogroms heighten tensions and spread violence across Palestinian territory.
items.summary: Al Jazeera reports that Israel arrested 36 Palestinians in the West Bank as attacks on farmers and their lands intensified during the olive harvest.

items.title: Five Israelis wounded and two suspected Palestinian attackers killed in West Bank shooting
items.snippet: The attack comes at a time of heightened tensions in the West Bank and four days before Israel's general election.
items.summary: The BBC reports that five Israelis were wounded and two suspected Palestinian attackers were killed in a West Bank shooting, amid heightened tensions and days before Israel's general election.
items.why: The incident’s location and timing place it within a period of heightened West Bank tensions.

items.title: Hospitals deliberately targeted by Sudan's RSF fighters, BBC finds
items.snippet: The UN human rights chief Volker Türk says the multiple attacks may amount to war crimes.
items.summary: A BBC investigation finds Sudan's RSF fighters deliberately targeted hospitals. The UN human rights chief says the multiple attacks may amount to war crimes.
items.why: The allegations highlight the strategic and humanitarian significance of attacks on hospitals in Sudan.

items.title: Ukraine says Starlink still restricted after Trump says limits lifted
items.snippet: Issues remain with the network used by the Ukrainian military, sources say, after repeated denials of a deliberate slowdown.
items.summary: The BBC reports that Trump says Musk restored Ukraine’s access after a Starlink dispute. It says Ukraine relies on Starlink for military uses, while Musk has denied restricting access.
items.why: Ukraine’s reliance on Starlink makes access to the service strategically relevant to its military.

items.title: Hundreds of flights cancelled as Typhoon Champi shuts Taiwan
items.snippet: One person has died after being swept away by waves in Taiwan's Liuqiu island, authorities say.
items.summary: Typhoon Champi shut Taiwan, with hundreds of flights cancelled. Authorities say one person died after being swept away by waves on Liuqiu island.
items.why: The cancellations indicate disruption to air travel across Taiwan during the typhoon.

learn.explainer: SQL injection is a flaw that can let attackers interfere with an application’s database queries. The VeloCloud Orchestrator item says its SQL injection flaw can expose privileged functionality.
IAMD means integrated air and missile defense: capabilities brought together to defend against air and missile threats. The item describes these capabilities as part of the proposed F110 frigate.
Sanctions are restrictions imposed by governments or other authorities. The Iran item says smartphones are reaching the country despite sanctions and trade restrictions.
